title: Dear as Thou Wert, and Justly Dear
description: Dear as Thou Wert, and Justly Dear in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Dale wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 594 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Death of a Christian”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear as thou wert, and just-ly dear, We will not weep for thee: One thought shall check the start-ing tear It is, that thou art free.

lines: Dear as thou wert, and justly dear,
We will not weep for thee:
One thought shall check the starting tear
It is, that thou art free.
And thus shall faith's consoling power
O, who that saw thy parting hour
Joy breathed in thy expiring sigh,
To think the race was run.
O, may such grace on us be shed,
And make our end like thine.

licence: Public domain: Thomas Dale died in 1870.
credits: Words by Thomas Dale (1797–1870), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
